newsitem.title: HONG KONG: New World, lots of cash on hand - chairman.
newsitem.headline: New World, lots of cash on hand - chairman.

text.p: Property developer New World Development Co Ltd has plenty of cash and no immediate need to raise finance although it would not rule out issuing another convertible bond, said managing director Henry Cheng.

"We have no definite plans for raising financing at the moment, because New World (Development) itself has a lot of cash on hand to cope with future development," said Cheng at a news conference on Tuesday.
About 15 months ago, the company issued a convertible bond, convertible into New World China shares if and when New World China was listed on Hong Kong exchange, said Cheng.
"Of course, we can not eliminate the possibility by doing some exercise like that," he said.
The group's most recent fund-raising exercise was a HK$1.5 billion credit facility arranged for New World PCS Ltd for the development and operation of that company's personal communication system.

The company announced its results for the first six months of financial year 1996/97 on Tuesday. It reported profit attributable to shareholders of HK$2.2 billion, a 29.2 percent increase over the corresponding period last year.
Subsidiary New World Infrastructure Ltd also announced its first-half results showing a 28 percent rise in attributable profit to HK$273.42 million.

In conjunction with the results, the company issued a statement giving the capital structure of the subsidiary and showing a rise in the debt to equity ratio of New World Infrastructure to 1.14 times, assuming the full draw down of a US$500 million syndicated loan.
As at end June 1997, the subsidiary had a debt to equity ratio of 0.55 times, the statement said.
